text:
anna: FYI saw a notable p95 regression on rtx-a pools after last night's autotune run. Pick telemetry looks suspicious for seq~1024.

mike: can you paste the pick lines?

anna: sure — enabling pick trace, grabbing a snippet. TL;DR: many requests are falling back to generic_gemm instead of arch_matmul_fast even when hw=ampere. reason codes look like 'capacity_estimate' or 'cache_mismatch'.

anna: sample log: 
```
PICK_TRACE ts=1864001234 req_id=abc123 model=gptx seq=1024 hw=ampere chosen=generic_gemm reason=capacity_estimate score=-0.12 conf=0.82 flags=[RDW_PICK_SAMPLING=0.01, RDW_KERNEL_DEBUG=1]
PICK_TRACE ts=1864001235 req_id=def456 model=gptx seq=1024 hw=ampere chosen=generic_gemm reason=kv_cache_mismatch score=-0.30 conf=0.45
PICK_TRACE ts=1864001240 req_id=ghi789 model=gptx seq=512 hw=ampere chosen=arch_matmul_fast reason=latency_budget score=0.75 conf=0.92
```

mike: interesting — two different reasons. capacity_estimate implies autotuner is pessimistic for longer seqs. kv_cache_mismatch suggests cache-size heuristics forcing a different execution path.

sara: also saw KV cache evictions around the same time (cache-stats spike). Might be workload skew: more long-context sessions hit simultaneously, cache warming falling behind. :eyes:

kevin: can you share the env flags you used for trace? I want to repro in staging.

anna: flags we turned on in prod trace: 
```
RDW_RUNTIME_PICK_TRACE=1
RDW_KERNEL_DEBUG=trace
RDW_PICK_SAMPLING=0.02
RDW_PICK_STRICT_ARCH=0  # autotune still allowed cross-arch fallbacks
RDW_KV_CACHE_PREFETCH=1
```

mike: two ideas: 1) bump RDW_PICK_STRICT_ARCH to 1 in a canary to favor arch-specific kernels when confidence close, 2) adjust capacity estimator to weight sequence-length histograms heavier.

sara: agree on canary. but watch KV prefetch interactions — prefetch=1 + strict_arch=1 might increase mem pressure on ampere devices. test memory footprint.

kevin: I'll spin a canary in eu-west1: create a dev group with seq distribution skewed to 1024 and run autotune with tracing enabled. can we add a pick-explain field to logs for the canary? something like pick_reason_details=\"estimator:0.6,cache:0.4\"

anna: good call. adding that to the trace now.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary/arch-strict-1 -> eu-west1 (3 nodes) by kevin. ETA ~6m.

mike: after canary, if we still see generic_gemm for seq=1024 with high latency, rollback autotune last-night change and mark it as regression. also add a perf-test with 1k seq_samples to CI.

sara: I'll correlate cache-eviction timestamps with pick traces and post a short csv.

kevin: canary started. collecting traces to gs://rdw-traces/1864001234-canary. will ping when finished.

anna: thanks — once we have pick_reason_details we can update the scoring function in autotuner to prefer arch_matmul_fast when score delta < 0.15 and seq_len>768.

mike: one last note — if KV fallback is the issue, we might add a cheap pre-check: if kv_cache_hit_ratio < 0.6 and seq_len>800, force a fallback to 'seq-slow' path intentionally to avoid thrashing. we should simulate before rolling out.

kevin: ack. will run the simulation and dump results.

anna: ok keeping this thread as tracker. tagging follow-ups: @mike (tuner), @sara (kv), @kevin (canary).

mike: thanks. will file a short postmortem if we end up reverting autotune.

sara: uploading cache csv now.

deploy-bot: canary report: 1864001300 records collected.

kevin: initial canary summary: arch_matmul_fast usage up from 48%->87% for seq>768, p95 improved 12%, but memory high on one node (OOM avoidance triggered). pausing rollout for memory check.

anna: perfect — that's evidence autotune tweak was too aggressive on memory heuristics. next steps: tune estimator and add mem-safety clamp.

mike: creating ticket: RT-kernelexplain-1864 to track estimator weight + mem clamp + CI perf test.

anna: thanks all. continuing in RT-kernelexplain-1864.
